name: Generala
description: Generala is a Cameroonian multi-player elimination card game played in tricks with a 54-card deck including two jokers. Players try to shed all cards; in each game the last player with cards is eliminated from the next game of the series.

overview.description: Generala is a Cameroonian multi-player elimination card game played in tricks with a 54-card deck including two jokers. Players try to shed all cards; in each game the last player with cards is eliminated from the next game of the series.

history.origins: First English rules were published in August 2011 from a report by Alexey Lobashev, who learned the game from Takam Ludovic Thierry; a corrected version was published in August 2012 after clarifying misunderstood trick and pickup rules. The game is a popular family game in Cameroon.
timeline: 2011: First English rules publication based on local player report.
2012: Corrected version published with clarified trick and pickup procedures.
Present: Continues in informal family and social play.
history.cultural: Generala functions as a social elimination series where a champion emerges after repeated games.
history.evolution: Published corrections focused on exact trick interruption and pickup behavior when a player cannot or does not follow suit.

setup.deck: One 54-card international pack with two jokers.
setup.dealing: Deal all cards one by one counterclockwise. Some players may receive one more card than others.

rules.objective: In each game, avoid being the last player still holding cards. Across a series, survive eliminations to become champion.
rules.gameplay: The player on dealer's right leads the first trick with the last card dealt to them. Players in counterclockwise order must follow led suit if possible. A player without led suit may play a joker if desired. If all active players contribute a card, trick is completed; highest card wins, and if jokers appear the first joker played is highest. If a player cannot follow and does not play a joker, trick ends immediately: later players do not play, that player picks one non-joker card from trick into hand, and remaining trick cards are set aside face down. Trick winner leads next trick (with special handling if winner just played final card and has no cards left). Players who empty hand drop out; play continues until one player still has cards.
keyRules: Follow suit is mandatory when possible.
Joker is highest rank and can be played when void; if joker is led, others may play any cards.
On interrupted tricks, picker cannot take a joker from the trick.
Series format eliminates the loser of each game; with two players each game is simply winner versus loser.

strategy.basic: Preserve suit flexibility to avoid forced interrupted-trick pickups.
strategy.intermediate: Use jokers to control lead changes and avoid becoming the likely picker in fragile tricks.
strategy.advanced: Track active players' likely void suits; choose leads that maximize chances opponents fail to follow without joker cover.
tips: Avoid wasting a joker into already-safe tricks when lead control is not critical.
When hand size shrinks, prioritize safe exits because timing of final-card plays affects who leads next.

variations.name: Series Elimination
variations.description: Standard multi-player form where loser of each game sits out next game until one champion remains.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation is the default series form; no engine overrides needed.

variations.name: Two-Player Loop
variations.description: With two players, each individual game has a winner and loser; loser deals next game.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Only deal rotation differs; no engine constant overrides.

scoring.description: Outcome is elimination-based: each game identifies one loser (last player with cards), and series continues with that player removed in multiplayer mode.
scoring.winCondition: Across series, be the last remaining player not eliminated.

synthesis.shortDescription: Counterclockwise trick-elimination game where hand exhaustion removes players and each game eliminates one loser.
